findings.title: The docs site never mentions states, the headline feature of 0.9
findings.summary: The README sends readers to lyr-ai.github.io/typedmem for docs. That site still opens with the pre-0.9 'Contract-driven memory' pitch, and no page on it documents set/get/history, StateConflict or --valid-from.
findings.failure_mode: A visitor who follows the README's Docs link finds a different product story and no documentation of the feature the README just showed them. The CLI reference describes `history` as it worked before v0.6.
impact: Anyone following the CLI reference for `history`
why_now: 0.9.0/0.9.1 released 2026-09-26 with states as the headline
Distribution of the changing-facts story is about to start
The explorer now lives on the same site

evidence.claim: Docs home still leads with the old positioning
CLI reference has no set/get sections; `history` is documented as the pre-v0.6 evolution_history trail
Concepts page says nothing closes a validity window automatically; for states, the resolver now ends a value where the next begins
No docs page mentions set_state, typedmem set/get or StateConflict
evidence.output: 0 matches in index.md, quickstart.md, cli.md, server.md, profiles.md, evolvers.md

evidence.claim: States landed without a docs change; docs/cli.md was last edited before them (2b78e8b)
README points readers at the docs site

findings.next_step: Add a 'States' page (set/get/history, the four outcomes, conflicts, --valid-from), fix the `history` entry in docs/cli.md, and align docs/index.md with the README's first screen.

findings.title: Issue #5 describes the gap 0.9's states now close, but is still open
findings.summary: Issue #5 (2026-09-14) records that a slot can't have both one governing value and a queryable past. The state type gives exactly that: a single current value plus history resolvable at any as_of. The issue isn't linked to design 0002.
findings.failure_mode: A prospective user scanning open issues concludes TypedMem can't keep a governing value with history, which is the product's main 0.9 promise.
impact: Credibility of the headline feature for issue-readers
why_now: Distribution starts now; open issues are part of what visitors read

evidence.claim: Open: 'a slot cannot have both one governing value and a queryable past'
resolve() gives one current value per key and resolves any as_of from full history
The issue was filed for fact/preference slots; it may deserve a note rather than closing, if those types are meant to stay as they are

findings.next_step: Comment on #5 linking design 0002 and states; close it or narrow it to the non-state types.

findings.title: list() can disagree with get() after a future-dated value takes effect
findings.summary: get/history resolve a state as of now; list/all() read the superseded_by index, which is only rewritten on the next set of that key.
findings.failure_mode: After a scheduled value's start passes, list() still shows the old value as active while get() returns the new one.
impact: Code that lists memories instead of calling get()
Only future-dated values; ordinary sets are consistent
why_now: Known and tracked (#7), with a strict xfail waiting to flip

evidence.claim: Reported with a reproduction
A strict xfail test documents the disagreement
The xfail still fails as expected

findings.next_step: Make list/all() resolve states as of now (as in #7); the xfail flips to a pass.

findings.title: `typedmem set` says '(unchanged)' when it confirms a past value
findings.summary: When a late record corroborates a value the state had in the past, the CLI prints 'key = Pro (unchanged)', which reads as if Pro is current.
findings.failure_mode: A user following the README's late-record story with a known past value believes the late record changed the current state.
impact: CLI users; the stored state itself is correct
why_now: The README's story is exactly this scenario

evidence.claim: Reported with commands and expected message
The unchanged branch prints the value without checking whether it is current

findings.next_step: Print 'Pro (from Apr 1) already recorded; source added; current is Enterprise' when the confirmed value isn't current.

findings.title: The HTTP server and TypeScript client can't use states
findings.summary: States exist only in Python and the CLI. Over HTTP, writing a state is refused (cleanly, with a 400) and there is no endpoint for get/history.
findings.failure_mode: Teams using the server or the TS client can't adopt the 0.9 feature at all.
why_now: Deliberately out of scope for 0.9; becomes relevant if a non-Python user shows up

evidence.claim: A state write over HTTP is refused with an explanation
The server's write path is add_memory only
Demand is unknown; build only when a real user asks

findings.next_step: None yet. Revisit when a non-Python user asks.

findings.title: CI doesn't smoke-run the demo the README links to
findings.summary: CI runs six example scripts but not agent_loop_demo.py, the 'before-vs-after agent story' linked from the README. It runs today.
findings.failure_mode: A future change breaks the linked demo and nothing notices.
impact: Readers who try the linked demo

evidence.claim: The demo step lists six scripts, not agent_loop_demo.py
The README links this demo
It runs cleanly today
evidence.output: 41 lines; ends 'the ability to debug its own behavior over time.'

findings.next_step: Add it to the smoke-run list.
